title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated video and synthetic likeness to create a false identity, not a failure of a legitimate AI deployment gone wrong. The failure mode is deliberate misuse: deepfake tools were used to produce convincing video of a real, named attorney and then distribute that content across social media platforms at scale, with hundreds of fake profiles created to reach a vulnerable population seeking immigration legal services. The harm occurred at the point of contact between victims and the fraudulent accounts, before any licensed professional or platform verification step intervened.

The scale of the operation, nearly 6,500 fake accounts removed across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, indicates that platform content moderation did not catch the fake profiles quickly or reliably. The scam reached victims through social media video, then moved them off-platform to WhatsApp for contracting and to payment apps for collection, a chain specifically designed to avoid any single point of institutional oversight. What it would have taken to catch this earlier is identity-verification or likeness-protection systems on the platforms where the fake accounts were seeded, or detection of coordinated inauthentic behavior across accounts promoting the same individual.

What is not established is who operated the scheme, where they are located, or whether any law enforcement investigation has produced findings or charges.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using his likeness to promote fraudulent immigration services. These deepfakes offer services such as US residency assistance for undocumented immigrants in exchange for payments like $2,200, along with fake testimonials from supposed former clients claiming successful legal outcomes. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office.

The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months, prompting Leal to hire an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Scammers typically direct victims through social media videos to WhatsApp, where they send phony contracts and request payment via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams. He warns immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to avoid anyone requesting immediate payment.
